quote: People can stand what is true,for they are already enduring it.
content: The litany is from a psychotherapy self-help manual, Gendlin's Focusing (1978, book, no DOI), and its central line is false for the class of truths that matter most to it. A person does not already endure a truth they do not know: the carrier of a Huntington's mutation who has not been tested is not enduring the diagnosis, and knowing it changes the experience of every subsequent year. That is why, when predictive testing became available, only a small minority of at-risk individuals chose it, and why the economics of information avoidance treats such choices as rational rather than as failures of nerve (Golman, Hagmann & Loewenstein 2017). "Owning up to it doesn't make it worse" is an empirical claim about hedonics, and for information that cannot be acted on, the evidence is that it sometimes does. The sequence adopts the litany as a law of psychology. It is a therapist's encouragement, useful for the cases it was written for, which are the ones where the truth is already being endured.
